# Notes for a paper draft (internal)

Method name: TideNet. A weight-shared recurrent operator for flood forecasting from sparse river gauges.
Problem: forecasters must predict water levels at ungauged points; physics solvers need full boundary data that is missing; learned models trained on one basin drift when rolled out for many days.
Mechanism: one recurrent cell is applied for T steps; a residual gate keeps the state fixed when the observation residual is zero; trained with T up to 16, evaluated up to T=128.
Results (single seed, internal card 012, exploratory; the final main table will be rerun with the finalized model and a unified recipe): NSE 0.81 vs 0.74 for a ConvLSTM baseline on 3 basins; at T=128 TideNet drops 0.02 while ConvLSTM drops 0.19.
Theory: Theorem 1 shows the zero-residual state is a fixed point; Theorem 2 bounds drift by the residual norm.
